title: Latency-Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt-5-mini
abstract: We preregistered (CAND-2026-001) and executed a paired confirmatory study evaluating whether a latency-aware selective verification tier (risk scoring + fast verifier) reduces unsafe commits from LLM-generated network-change proposals while satisfying an operational latency SLO. Using a deterministic synthetic 400-intent corpus (10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a deterministic full-checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) as ground truth, we observed baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975) and guarded (selective verifier) valid = 400/400 (1.000). The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). All raw outputs, per-episode scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256s in the execution manifest; key artifact examples and hashes are cited in the Disclosure Statement. The preregistered latency hypothesis (95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms) could not be evaluated because end-to-end latency telemetry is absent from the archived confirmatory artifacts; this absence is disclosed rather than imputed.

sections.introduction: Motivation and research question. Automating intent→configuration translation promises operational efficiency but raises safety risks: generated proposals can violate invariants or introduce regressions. A pragmatic architecture is generate→validate→repair: an LLM proposes changes, a verifier adjudicates functional correctness, and repairs iterate when needed. Full verification provides strong safety but can be slow; operators may accept a selective fast-verifier that only checks high-risk proposals. We preregistered CAND-2026-001 to test (H1) whether a selective low-latency verification tier reduces unsafe commits relative to LLM-only (paired design, same intent presented to both conditions), and (H2) whether the selective pipeline meets a preregistered latency SLO (95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms). The preregistration (CAND-2026-001) froze design, estimands, sampling plan, retry/missingness rules, and analysis scripts before execution (preregistration SHA-256: 086d248e89636e99e788232e78a99b63459648545e6e79ed763c29521f8f8572).
sections.related_work: Positioning. Recent work has demonstrated verifier-augmented LLM configuration repair (e.g., Cornetto-style benchmarks and agentic verifier pipelines) and agentic NetOps architectures combining LLM agents with digital twins and formal checkers. Those studies show verifiers reduce regressions but often omit latency-safety trade-offs under operational budgets. Our contribution is an artifact-backed, preregistered paired evaluation that (i) records complete provenance (model calls, scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider logs) with SHA‑256s; (ii) reconciles planned vs observed provider call accounting under a shared-initial candidate design; and (iii) reports exact paired inference and bootstrap CIs traceable to archived artifacts.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and experiment design. Preregistered elements (CAND-2026-001): study ID, research question, confirmatory hypotheses (H1,H2), primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, sampling plan (N=400 paired intents; 10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants), fixed random seeds, retry and missingness rules, analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), and multiplicity plan. Execution contract: adapter_family=hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model=gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json, SHA-256: a40e96e2...); transformation: shared_initial_candidate reused across conditions (independent_condition_generation=false) so each intent produced one shared candidate that both conditions evaluated (reduces generation variance and model-call cost; preregistered). Task bank and generator: deterministic synthetic operator-intent corpus covering representative change classes (ACLs, routing edits, interface edits); task manifests, reference answers, and validator rules are archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl. Validator and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implemented the full-checker (scorer rule full_intent_constraint_validation); per-episode scorer JSONs and validator traces are archived at execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ (SHA‑256s in the execution manifest). Analysis plan: primary test = exact McNemar two-sided on paired binary correctness; paired bootstrap percentile CIs (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) for the paired difference; sensitivity analyses for infrastructure failures per preregistered missingness plan. Reproducibility: all calls, retries, logs, and artifacts archived with hashes (execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.results: Execution and primary outcomes (artifact-backed). Run summary: planned confirmatory pairs = 400; completed pairs = 400; model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial generations + 1 repair) — the observed call count and stage_counts are recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json and reconciled deterministically (see deterministic_reconciliation.json). Primary outcomes: baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975); guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). Contingency table (guarded × baseline): n11=399, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA-256 a6906bb4...). Estimand (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). All per-episode scorer JSONs and validator traces are archived (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256 ea8359d..., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA-256 431f61c0...; the single discordant pair is available at execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (SHA-256: fe147f43...) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (SHA-256: d0cbfe9a...); these files show the baseline proposal failed a dependency check while the guarded pipeline selected or produced a corrected candidate).
sections.discussion: Interpretation, operational implications, and threats. Interpretation: the guarded intervention produced a small absolute safety gain (0.25 percentage points) over an already near-ceiling baseline (399→400). The observed effect is artifact-backed but numerically small and not statistically significant under McNemar; the paired bootstrap CI quantifies uncertainty. Ceiling effects: with baseline correctness ≈99.75% the experiment has limited headroom to demonstrate large verifier gains — a preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline ≈8% unsafe rate and targeted a 5 percentage-point improvement; the synthetic corpus realized much higher baseline correctness, reducing power. Design choice consequences: the preregistered shared-initial candidate protocol isolates verifier/repair impact conditional on a single LLM candidate and dramatically reduced model-call cost (401 observed calls vs a possible 800 under independent generation). This choice should be considered when generalizing to workflows where independent candidate generation per approval path is required. Latency SLO (H2) unresolved: preregistered H2 required end-to-end timing telemetry; the archived confirmatory artifacts lack end-to-end latency traces, so H2 cannot be evaluated from this run — the absence and its provenance are logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. Threats to validity: (i) internal: shared-initial design and single-model choice; (ii) construct: deterministic validator abstracts device semantics; (iii) external: synthetic corpus and single LLM limit generality; (iv) conclusion: near-ceiling baseline reduces detectable effect size. Recommendations: future runs should (1) record end-to-end latency telemetry (timestamps at generation, risk-scoring, fast verifier, full-checker) to evaluate H2; (2) repeat with independent_condition_generation=true to estimate joint generation+verifier effects; (3) sweep selective-verifier thresholds on larger OOD/adversarial sets to map verification-budget vs unsafe-commit Pareto frontiers; (4) test multiple LLMs and validators. All recommendations are implementable within the same artifact pipeline: per-episode scorer JSONs, provider-call logs, and execution manifest already support these extensions.
sections.conclusion: We report a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation of a selective low-latency verification intervention for LLM-generated NetOps changes. The guarded pipeline produced a numerically small safety improvement over a very strong baseline (399→400 valid proposals). The result is fully traceable to archived artifacts (responses, per-episode scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider-call logs, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts with SHA‑256s). The preregistered latency objective (H2) could not be evaluated because end-to-end latency telemetry was not archived; this absence is disclosed and logged. The study demonstrates the practicalities and provenance requirements for rigorous NetOps-AI evaluation and identifies concrete, artifact-grounded next steps to evaluate latency–safety trade-offs and to generalize across models and real operator language.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement (artifact-backed):
- Initial master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The Research Director provided the topic family and initial constraints before the autonomy lock; all study formulation, preregistration, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revisions were performed autonomously after the lock as required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track.
- Preregistration: CAND-2026-001 preregistration artifact (SHA-256: 086d248e89636e99e788232e78a99b63459648545e6e79ed763c29521f8f8572) froze hypotheses H1/H2, estimands, sampling plan (N=400 paired intents; 10% adversarial), retry and missingness rules, analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), and multiplicity plan prior to observing outcomes.
- Model(s) and configuration: declared generator = gpt-5-mini. Model configuration and declared parameters archived at execution/model_configuration.json (SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; provider traces and per-call logs archived (execution/provider_calls/*.json; see execution manifest hashes).
- Orchestration and transformation: the preregistered execution contract specified independent_condition_generation=false (shared-initial candidate) so each intent produced one shared candidate reused across conditions. This design choice was preregistered and deterministically enacted; it explains the observed model call accounting (model_calls_used = 401) versus the naive planned budget of 800. Reconciliation and provider-call stage counts are archived in execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (see those artifacts and SHA‑256s in the manifest).
- Validator and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implemented the full-checker used as ground truth for per-episode validation and scoring under scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Per-episode scorer JSONs are archived in execution/scoring/ (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256: ea8359d..., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA-256: 431f61c0...). Per-episode validator traces are archived under execution/responses/ (examples: execution/responses/task-000001-baseline.txt SHA-256: 8f38c8be...); all file paths and SHA-256s are listed in the execution manifest.
- Execution accounting and provenance: the run completed 800 episodes (400 paired intents × 2 conditions) as planned, producing 400 paired scores. Observed model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared initial + 1 repair). The exact provider-call audit, stage_counts, and per-call logs are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and summarized in execution/execution_manifest.json (artifact SHA‑256s included). The analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json documents that the shared-initial design was used and that all deterministic consistency checks passed.
- Statistical analysis: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; test = exact McNemar two-sided; paired bootstrap percentile CI computed with 10,000 resamples and seed 1729. Analysis artifacts (paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256: a6906bb4..., condition_summary.csv SHA-256: 0d6efc16...) and analysis log are archived under analysis/ with SHA‑256s.
- Missing or unresolved preregistered items: preregistered H2 required end-to-end latency telemetry (95th-percentile comparison). The archived confirmatory artifact bundle does not contain end-to-end latency traces; this prevents artifact-backed evaluation of H2. The absence is logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (artifact SHA‑256s in the execution manifest). We disclose this missing telemetry and do not impute latency.
- Human involvement: no human manual editing of technical content, analysis, or manuscript text occurred after the autonomy lock. Pre-lock human work was limited to selecting the topic family and approving the initial master prompt and infrastructure rehearsal; pre-lock artifacts and development runs were not used as confirmatory empirical evidence unless recreated post-lock (they were not).
- Reproducibility: all raw outputs, per-episode scorer JSONs, response texts, provider-call traces, task and transformation manifests, model configuration, execution manifest, result schema, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes and paths in execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis artifacts. Representative artifact locations and SHA‑256s are cited above (e.g., execution/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256: a6906bb4..., analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256: 0d6efc16..., execution/execution_log.jsonl SHA‑256: 421f8e68..., analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256: 9ea0d56d...). Independent auditors can use these immutable file references to reproduce the deterministic reconciliation and the reported statistics.
limitations: Synthetic confirmatory corpus: tasks were generated deterministically; linguistic and operational diversity of production operator intents is not represented.
Single-model evaluation: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not generalize across LLM families without further runs.
Deterministic validator abstraction: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 models network semantics in a digital-twin; real-device divergences remain possible.

Shared-initial design conditionality: independent_condition_generation=false conditions the estimand on a single shared candidate per intent, narrowing the causal scope relative to independent-generation workflows.
Latency SLO unresolved: end-to-end timing telemetry required to evaluate H2 is absent from archived confirmatory artifacts and therefore H2 is unresolved for this run.
